title: introduce-context-aware-load-profile-drift-detector-and-autoscaler-guard
author: Leah Kim
description: Motivation: existing canary detectors focus on post-hoc latency/throughput regressions and percentile shifts; they have limited visibility into upstream changes in request composition and concurrency (load profile) that can silently drive apparent regressions or mask true regressions. This PR implements a context-aware load-profile drift detector that tracks multivariate request-shape features (input token length distribution, concurrency histogram, model route mix, and batch size distribution) and raises structured alerts when the running distribution deviates from baseline beyond an adaptive threshold. Design: 1) lightweight feature extractor executed at the per-route aggregator to emit compact sketches (q-digests and histograms) for token-length and latency-by-context; 2) drift scorer combines KL-like divergence for categorical route mix with Wasserstein-like distance for numeric features, weighted by recent token cost and route importance; 3) integrate a new "autoscaler_guard" rollout policy: when drift is detected concurrently with increased autoscaler activity, the platform will temporarily widen canary thresholds and attach a deterministic health tag to decisions to avoid cascading rollbacks due to load shaping; 4) add backfill mode for historical baseline recompute and an explainability payload that surfaces the top contributing features for triage. Implementation notes: detector implemented in perf-canary service (Go) and provides a protobuf-compatible alert payload consumed by canary-orchestrator; storage of compact sketches uses existing windowed metrics backend (Prometheus histograms + a small Redis index for sketches) to avoid new stateful services. Testing & validation: synthetic workload generator added to perf-canary/test/ with controlled shifts in token length and route mix; unit tests for scorer functions and end-to-end smoke harness runs against local canary-orchestrator. Rollout plan: feature gated behind config flag perf_canary.load_profile_drift.enabled=false by default; staged rollout to dev -> staging -> prod with canary windows of 5m/15m/1h; ops playbook included for interpreting explainability payload. Checklist: Closes ENG-4210; add unit/integration tests; add documentation and playbook; verify CI green; coordinate with infra for minor Redis index. Related: complements percentile-based detectors by offering early detection of input-shape-driven regressions and prevents unnecessary rollbacks during autoscaler transients.

review_conversation: Asha Patel: Great direction. Can you clarify the expected cardinality and retention of the Redis index? Ops will want limits hard-coded.
Leah Kim: Index stores O(routes * windows) sketches; default retention 6 hours; added caps and eviction policy + config knobs in new commit b4c2d09.
Marcus Liu: How sensitive is the scorer to short-lived spikes? Could we add a minimum sample count or debounce?
Leah Kim: Yes—added an adaptive debounce that increases window length when sample count < 200 and added a tunable min_samples config; see scorer.go changes.
Samir Nair: We should make the autoscaler guard opt-in per-namespace. Otherwise we risk hiding real regressions.
Leah Kim: Done: autoscaler_guard has namespace allowlist and global override; documented in playbook.
Asha Patel: CI flaky on first run due to test_e2e_drift timing; re-run fixed it. Approved after fixes.
Marcus Liu: LGTM, please squash and merge with release note entry.
ci_checks: integration-tests: pass (one re-run due to timing flake)
merge: squash-merge by Marcus Liu; merge commit 7c3a2b8; release notes added to changelog under perf-canary: Introduced a context-aware load profile drift detector with an autoscaler-aware rollout guard to reduce noisy rollbacks and surface input-shape regressions.
release_notes: Add context-aware load-profile drift detector (perf-canary). Detects shifts in token length distribution, route mix, concurrency; includes autoscaler_guard to avoid false rollbacks during scaling activity; gated behind feature flag; docs and ops playbook included.
notes_for_ops: Default config keeps detector disabled in prod. When enabled start in dev and staging; monitor "drift_alerts_total" and "drift_top_features" dashboards; if autoscaler_guard expands thresholds excessively, revert namespace allowlist or disable autoscaler integration; Redis index is capped and will evict oldest sketches under pressure.
